def r_layout_column_wrap(*args, width="200px", fixed_width=False, heights_equal="all", fill=True, fillable=True, height=None, height_mobile=None, min_height=None, max_height=None, gap=None, **kwargs): """ Python implementation of bslib::layout_column_wrap This function creates a responsive grid layout with column wrapping. Since we're working with a simplified test environment, we return a string representation that captures the essential structure. """ # Validate heights_equal argument if heights_equal not in ("all", "row"): raise ValueError("heights_equal must be 'all' or 'row'") # Process children and attributes from *args children = list(args) attribs = kwargs.copy() # Handle deprecated positional width argument # Check if first child looks like a CSS unit (string) if len(children) > 0 and width == "200px": # width is still at default first_child = children[0] if isinstance(first_child, str): # Check if it looks like a CSS unit if _is_probably_a_css_unit(first_child): width = first_child children = children[1:] # Validate width length if not isinstance(width, (str, int, float)) or (isinstance(width, (list, tuple)) and len(width) > 1): raise ValueError("`width` of length greater than 1 is not currently supported.") # Build colspec (grid-template-columns) colspec = None if width is not None: width_val = width if isinstance(width_val, (int, float)): if width_val > 0 and width_val <= 1: num_cols = 1 / width_val if num_cols != int(num_cols): raise ValueError("Could not interpret width argument; see ?layout_column_wrap") colspec = f"repeat({int(num_cols)}, minmax(0, 1fr))" else: validated_width = _validate_css_unit(str(width_val)) if fixed_width: colspec = f"repeat(auto-fit, {validated_width})" else: colspec = f"repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min({validated_width}, 100%), 1fr))" else: validated_width = _validate_css_unit(width_val) if fixed_width: colspec = f"repeat(auto-fit, {validated_width})" else: colspec = f"repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min({validated_width}, 100%), 1fr))" # Build style string style_parts = [] if colspec: style_parts.append(f"grid-template-columns:{colspec}") if heights_equal == "all": style_parts.append("grid-auto-rows:1fr") validated_height = _validate_css_unit(height if height is not None else "auto") style_parts.append(f"--bslib-grid-height:{validated_height}") validated_height_mobile = _validate_css_unit(height_mobile if height_mobile is not None else "auto") style_parts.append(f"--bslib-grid-height-mobile:{validated_height_mobile}") if gap is not None: validated_gap = _validate_css_unit(gap) style_parts.append(f"gap:{validated_gap}") if min_height is not None: validated_min_height = _validate_css_unit(min_height) style_parts.append(f"min-height:{validated_min_height}") if max_height is not None: validated_max_height = _validate_css_unit(max_height) style_parts.append(f"max-height:{validated_max_height}") style_str = ";".join(style_parts) # Build class string classes = ["bslib-grid", "bslib-mb-spacing"] if fill: classes.append("html-fill-item") if kwargs.get("class"): classes.append(kwargs["class"]) class_str = " ".join(classes) # Build the HTML structure children_html = "".join(str(child) for child in children) grid_div = f'
{children_html}

\n {grid_div}\n
' return result def _is_probably_a_css_unit(val): """Check if a value looks like a CSS unit string.""" if not isinstance(val, str): return False # Simple heuristic: contains numbers and common CSS units css_units = ("px", "em", "rem", "pt", "%", "vh", "vw", "ex", "ch") return any(unit in val.lower() for unit in css_units) def _validate_css_unit(val): """Validate and normalize a CSS unit value.""" if val is None or val == "auto": return "auto" val_str = str(val) # Simple passthrough - in real R this does more validation return val_str

### Name: layout_column_wrap
### Title: Column-first uniform grid layouts
### Aliases: layout_column_wrap

### ** Examples

## Don't show: 
if (rlang::is_interactive()) withAutoprint({ # examplesIf
## End(Don't show)
x <- card("A simple card")

# Always has 2 columns (on non-mobile)
layout_column_wrap(width = 1/2, x, x, x)

# Automatically lays out three cards into columns
# such that each column is at least 200px wide:
layout_column_wrap(x, x, x)

# To use larger column widths by default, set `width`.
# This example has 3 columns when the screen is at least 900px wide:
layout_column_wrap(width = "300px", x, x, x)

# You can add a list of items, spliced with rlang's `!!!` operator
layout_column_wrap(!!!list(x, x, x))
## Don't show: 
}) # examplesIf
## End(Don't show)

# calls recorded from these examples and this script:
layout_column_wrap(width = "300px", x, x, x)
layout_column_wrap(width = 1/2, x, x, x)
layout_column_wrap(x, x, x)
